### CHUNK-000: fix-threading-regression
- **Kind**: `investigate`
- **Originating finding**: Preflight discovery (CHUNK-001) — `test/apertured.jl:66` accuracy assertion fails because per-frame deformation outputs are collapsed.
- **Cluster**: baseline-blocker
- **Breaking**: no (bug fix)
- **Description**: Find and fix the bug that causes every frame's `u` (and likely `:warped`, `:mismatch`) to be overwritten by a single frame's result when running under the threaded driver. Likely lives in either `RegisterDriver.driver` (per-tindex output routing) or in this package's `worker(::Apertures, img, tindex, mon)` (whether `mon` is per-thread vs. shared). Add a regression test that runs ≥2 distinct frames and asserts they recover distinct deformations.
- **Depends on**: none
- **Verification**: `test/apertured.jl:66` passes; new regression test in this package or RegisterDriver
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Notes**: Root cause: `RegisterWorkerShell.monitor(algorithms::Vector, fields, morevars)` was implemented as `map(alg -> monitor(alg, fields, morevars), algorithms)`. The single-algorithm form copies `morevars` keys/values directly into the per-algorithm mon, so every per-algorithm mon ended up pointing to **the same** preallocated `:u` and `:warped` buffers. Under the multi-threaded driver in `RegisterDriver.driver`, threads called `monitor!(mon, :u, ϕ.u)` (which does `copyto!(mon[:u], ϕ.u)`) in parallel on the shared buffer. The driver's `deepcopy(tmp)` snapshotted whatever was in the buffer at that moment — typically all frames saw the last-writer's value. Fix in `RegisterWorkerShell/src/RegisterWorkerShell.jl`: `map(alg -> monitor(alg, fields, deepcopy(morevars)), algorithms)`. Regression test added to `RegisterWorkerShell/test/runtests.jl` (asserts per-worker `mons[i][:buf] !== mons[j][:buf]`). Full RegisterWorkerApertures suite passes after fix. Fix is **uncommitted in RegisterWorkerShell** as of session close. This package's `test/apertured.jl:66` already provides cross-package regression coverage (asserts distinct per-frame deformations).

### CHUNK-004: align-tid-workertid
- **Kind**: `implement`
- **Originating finding**: T3-1 — constructor keyword `tid` stores into field `workertid`; the mismatch is confusing.
- **Cluster**: api-surface
- **Breaking**: yes — renames the struct field from `workertid` to `tid`; any external code accessing `algorithm.workertid` directly will break.
- **Description**: Rename the struct field `workertid` → `tid` in the `Apertures` definition (line 13 area) and update all internal references. The constructor keyword already uses `tid`, so no call-site change is needed.
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001
- **Verification**: tests pass; `grep -r workertid src/ test/` returns nothing
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Notes**: Renamed `workertid::Int` → `tid::Int` in the `Apertures` struct. Added `workertid(alg::Apertures) = alg.tid` override (imported from RegisterWorkerShell) so the protocol accessor still works. Also fixed RegisterDriver to call `workertid(alg)` instead of `alg.workertid` directly (two sites in `driver`), and added `workertid` to RegisterDriver's import of RegisterWorkerShell. RegisterWorkerShell's default `workertid(w::AbstractWorker) = w.workertid` is unchanged — it still works for all other AbstractWorker subtypes with a `workertid` field. Tests pass; `Test.detect_ambiguities` = 0. Changes are unstaged across three repos: RegisterWorkerApertures `src/`, RegisterDriver `src/`.

### CHUNK-005: remove-phantom-T
- **Kind**: `implement`
- **Originating finding**: T1-1 — `T` type parameter on `Apertures{A,T,K,N}` is always `Float64` (hard-coded in the outer constructor due to Ipopt's requirement). The parameter is misleading: users cannot construct an `Apertures` with `T≠Float64`.
- **Cluster**: api-surface
- **Breaking**: yes — changes the type identity of `Apertures`; code that dispatches on or constructs `Apertures{A,Float64,K,N}` explicitly will break.
- **Description**: Remove `T` from the type parameter list. Replace all internal uses of `T` as an element-type stand-in with the concrete `Float64`. Update the `AffinePenalty{T,N}` field type to `AffinePenalty{Float64,N}`. Add a one-line comment in the struct definition noting that `Float64` is fixed by the Ipopt requirement.
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001
- **Verification**: tests pass; `Test.detect_ambiguities` count unchanged or reduced; no `{A,T,K,N}` references remain
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Notes**: Removed `T` from `Apertures{A,T,K,N}` → `Apertures{A,K,N}`. Field types updated: `AffinePenalty{T,N}` → `AffinePenalty{Float64,N}`, `Union{T,Tuple{T,T}}` → `Union{Float64,Tuple{Float64,Float64}}`, `thresh::T` → `thresh::Float64` (comment noting Ipopt requirement). Constructor updated: removed `T = Float64` local, replaced all `T(...)` casts and `{...,T,...}` type applications with `Float64`. The `T` in `cuda_init!` is a separate local variable (`cuda_eltype(eltype(fixed))`) for the CUDA element type — left unchanged. No `{A,T,K,N}` references remain in source or tests. Tests pass; `detect_ambiguities` = 0.
